content: 1. The use of lorlatinib can reduce the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes in the liver and intestines. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. When a CYP3A4 inducer is added or discontinued, monitor the response to estrogens and progestins and adjust hormone dosages as necessary. For effective contraception, advise the use of additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods during coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers and for approximately three plasma half-lives after discontinuation. 2. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with weak CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor closely for arrhythmias or cardiac events, as the effect of lonafarnib on the QT interval is unknown. 3. Lopinavir can increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 4. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor can decrease the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 5. Mavacamten can decrease the systemic exposure of ethinylestradiol and progestin, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients should use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 6. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the effects of metyrapone by an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to a subtherapeutic response. Discontinuation of estrogens, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. 7. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 8. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Patients should consider using an alternative or additional form of contraception. 10. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 11. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may be less effective, and nonhormonal methods should be used. 13. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 14. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 16. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 17. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 18. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 20. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 21. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 23. Sugammadex decreases the effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by receptor binding competition. A bolus dose of sugammadex is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients must use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods (e.g., condoms and spermicides) for seven days after sugammadex administration. 24. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 26. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control during coadministration. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 27. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with hormonal contraceptives. If unavoidable, use additional effective nonhormonal contraceptive methods during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 28. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 29. Ethinylestradiol may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics, such as albiglutide, by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 30. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of coadministered benzodiazepines. 32. Concomitant use of ethinylestradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Use caution and monitor. 33. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
